intro.heading: Native modules
intro.summary: Limen separates its platform core, graphics backends, and GPU postprocessing into native libraries. This guide explains what each library does, when it loads, and which files to ship with your app.
module-list.heading: What each module does
module-list.intro: The core manages windows and OS integration. A graphics backend supplies the renderer API for a specific GPU technology. Postprocessing modules add optional features to a compatible renderer.
module-list.module.limen-hdll.descriptio: The SDL3 platform core: windows, displays, input, events, clipboard, and other system services. It also loads the other Limen modules.
module-list.module.opengl-limen.descript: Creates an OpenGL context for a window and exposes OpenGL operations, such as compiling shaders, binding textures, and drawing.
module-list.module.vulkan-limen.descript: Creates Vulkan surfaces and contexts and exposes explicit GPU control through queues, command buffers, and resource synchronization.
module-list.module.d3d11-limen.descripti: Direct3D 11 on Windows: device, swapchain, and rendering commands through the D3D11 device context.
module-list.module.d3d12-limen.descripti: Direct3D 12 on Windows x64: explicit control over command queues, descriptor heaps, and resource states.
module-list.module.dlss-limen.descriptio: NVIDIA Streamline integration on Windows x64. Upscaling on D3D11, D3D12, and Vulkan; frame generation on D3D12.
module-list.module.fsr-limen.description: AMD FidelityFX integration on Windows x64. Upscaling on D3D12 and Vulkan; frame generation and Anti-Lag 2 on D3D12.
loading.heading: How loading works
loading.paragraph: HashLink loads limen.hdll for Limen's Haxe native bindings. The core initializes SDL3 and, if graphics are enabled, uses SDL's dynamic loader to open the selected .limen library. A .limen file is a native shared library under a Limen-specific extension.
loading.abi: The graphics bindings still go through limen.hdll. For a backend call, the core looks up an hlp_* export in the corresponding module. The export supplies the function pointer and its HashLink signature. This lets Limen split and load its native code without adding a .limen loader to HashLink.
loading.lifecycle: Limen caches module load attempts and function lookups. To shut down, release graphics and postprocessing resources, destroy the windows, then call Platform.quit() to shut down SDL and unload the modules.
selection.heading: Choosing a graphics backend
selection.paragraph: Platform.init() prefers OpenGL by default. Pass GraphicsDriver.None to use windows, input, and other platform services without loading a renderer. With graphics enabled, the second argument lists the backends your app implements; omitting it allows all four. Limen tries the preferred backend if allowed, then tries the remaining allowed backends in this order: OpenGL → Vulkan → D3D11 → D3D12. The order of the array does not change that priority.
selection.example: This example logs the selected backend. It tries Vulkan first, can fall back to OpenGL, and never tries Direct3D. To require a single backend, put only that backend in the array. If Limen cannot load any allowed backend, initialization throws No LIMEN graphics driver was found.
selection.note.title: Loading a library and creating a renderer are separate steps
selection.note.paragraph: Read Platform.graphicsDriver before choosing window flags and creating a context or device. Limen shares the platform layer across renderers, but each backend has its own rendering API. A library that loads may still fail to create a device on the current hardware; the fallback in Platform.init() does not handle that later failure.
postprocess.heading: Optional GPU postprocessing
postprocess.paragraph: DLSS and FSR run on top of an existing graphics backend. Their temporal upscalers reconstruct a larger output image from lower resolution color, depth, motion vectors, and frame data. Both integrations share PostProcessDevice, TextureResource, and CommandBuffer, while keeping their own settings and setup steps.
postprocess.dlss: DLSS: Build with LIMEN_BUILD_DLSS=ON and point LIMEN_STREAMLINE_SDK_ROOT at the NVIDIA Streamline SDK. Ship the Streamline and NVIDIA runtime DLLs that the build packages. Initialize Streamline before creating the graphics interfaces it needs to configure.
postprocess.fsr: FSR: Build with LIMEN_BUILD_FSR=ON using MSVC. The D3D12 implementation links the FidelityFX SDK into the module; the Vulkan implementation needs amd_fidelityfx_vk.dll and exposes temporal upscaling only.
postprocess.availability: Selecting a renderer does not load its optional postprocessing modules. After Platform.init(), use DLSS.isAvailable() or FSR.isAvailable() to check whether the module can load and supports the selected backend. After setting up the provider, check support for the specific feature on your device before enabling it. Keep the normal rendering path available when the feature cannot be used.

where.heading: Which files to ship
where.paragraph: Find the native binaries under build/bin/<platform>-<configuration>. Use matching binaries for your target OS, architecture, and HashLink runtime. Follow the installation guide for the runtime layout and keep the required dependency DLLs from the build package.
where.platform: Windowing and input only: Use Platform.init(GraphicsDriver.None). Of the Limen modules, you only need limen.hdll.
where.single: One backend: Ship limen.hdll and its renderer module. For D3D12, also include dxcompiler.dll and dxil.dll from the build package.
where.fallback: Several backends: Ship the renderer modules your app can actually use, plus only the postprocessing modules and runtime DLLs for the features it offers.
where.troubleshooting: If graphics initialization reports that no driver was found, check the allowed backend list, the module's location and architecture, and its native dependencies. A module can fail to load even when the file is present if a library it depends on is missing.
